title: Ascending Flags
description: Economy architecture, a 40+ card catalog and cross-discipline leadership on a competitive card game at Scary Noodles.

items.label: Gameplay systems
items.body: Architected the core combat and resource economy models, running parallel balancing loops to keep dominant strategies out and competitive health in.

items.label: Card design
items.body: Conceived and balanced a 40+ card catalog for archetypal synergy, mechanical variety and strategic depth.

items.label: Direct reports
items.body: Drove production roadmaps across art, design and engineering, keeping the pipeline collaborative and the milestones clean.

items.label: Playtest iteration
items.body: Validated the competitive loop through paper prototyping before deployment, which took the technical risk out early.

blocks.html: I acted as the central vision holder across design, programming and art — mentoring team members, unblocking cross-discipline dependencies, and keeping product goals aligned so the mechanics and the creative stayed coherent.

I owned the foundational system loops, using analog paper testing to refine pacing. The pivotal call was eliminating split movement currencies: movement, utility and offensive actions all draw on a single resource pool, so every turn is an economic trade-off and inefficient play is punished on its own terms.

blocks.caption: One mana pool funds every action. Surplus terrain converts back to mana, so the economy keeps flowing without dead draws.

items.label: Imperfect information
items.body: Concealed enemy flag positions and base parameters, which raises the strategic value of scouting and makes bluffing worth doing.

items.label: Variance mitigation
items.body: Excess terrain cards convert into usable mana once the board is saturated, eliminating late-game dead draws.

items.label: Asymmetric border placement
items.body: Hidden flag deployment along personalised territory boundaries, so opponents have to deduce coordinates from movement cues.
